summary: The reports are technically strong and the numerical, formula, protocol, resource, and image checks passed, but two related-work rows fail the required bibliographic metadata check: DriveZero is attributed to a project team instead of the paper authors, and DVGT omits its formal CVPR 2026 publication state and formal source.

findings.finding: The related-work row identifies DriveZero as authored by 'Xiaomi EV AD & Robotics L3 Team'. That is a valid project/team label, but it is not the formal author attribution of the arXiv paper. The fixed arXiv record lists Hao He followed by 19 coauthors. The row therefore does not satisfy the report template's requirement to record verified related-work authors.
findings.evidence: The arXiv metadata names Hao He, Chengcheng Hu, Zirun Su, Heng Zhang, Haisong Liu, Jinke Li, Haochen Tian, Zhenwei Shen, Hongyang Li, Zhichao Li, Yunchen Yang, Bochao Huang, Siyu Zhang, Kuangye Chen, Xiongjie Zhang, Wentao Dai, Hengchen Dai, Siyuan Liu, Zehao Huang, and Naiyan Wang; the project page separately brands the work as an AD & Robotics, L3 Team technical report.
findings.fix: Change the row label to 'Hao He 等（Xiaomi EV AD & Robotics L3 Team），DriveZero，2026 年技术报告/arXiv 预印本' and keep the current mechanism comparison. Add the arXiv abstract link as the metadata source while retaining the project page if team attribution is useful.

findings.finding: The DVGT row describes a 2025 arXiv first version and a 2026 revision but omits that DVGT is a formally published CVPR 2026 paper. This is not merely unavailable metadata: the ViRA paper's own bibliography cites DVGT as 'In CVPR, 2026', and the CVF Open Access paper is available.
findings.evidence: The CVF formal paper lists Sicheng Zuo et al. and CVPR 2026. The checked ViRA v1 PDF bibliography also records 'DVGT: Driving visual geometry transformer. In CVPR, 2026a.'
findings.fix: Change the row label to 'Zuo 等，DVGT，CVPR 2026' and add the CVF formal-paper link before the fixed arXiv v2 section link. The mechanism description can remain unchanged.

figureChecks.check: Teacher has current plus recorded-future views; student has current views only; the bottom panels depict diverse target selection and unsafe/safe score correction. Caption and report interpretation match the official image.
Three rows show NC/DAC, TTC, and progress examples; the image contains FPD mean/p99 latency 88.4/98.0 ms and DrivoR 58.2/58.5 ms. The report correctly treats these as selected examples.
The frozen VFM is training-only, the policy consumes planner features, and the lower panels correspond to spatial KL and bidirectional semantic alignment.
The report correctly reads the 36.4 mIoU baseline and the distinct 83.6/82.6 EPDMS baselines for with/without perception supervision before converting gains to absolute values.
The official asset depicts SGS, SCTA, and ESA. The fixed PDF labels it Figure 2 while the HTML labels the same asset Figure 1 because the PDF teaser is omitted from HTML.
The official asset has GT/Ours/ALOcc/STCOcc columns, flow colors, red direction arrows, and green interaction ellipses. The fixed PDF and HTML numbering differs exactly as the report states.

fpdPaperVersusRepositoryScoresAndSteps.paper: Fixed arXiv v1 reports Base 94.9/55.9 and Pro 95.5/58.1 for NAVSIM v1/v2, with eight default DDIM steps and a 2/4/6/8/12-step ablation ending at 94.9/94.9.
fpdPaperVersusRepositoryScoresAndSteps.repository: The current README reports Base 94.88/54.75 and Pro 95.57/58.07. All four inspected inference YAML files set num_inference_steps=12 and full_history_status=false.
fpdPaperVersusRepositoryScoresAndSteps.reportHandling: The report preserves both sources, calls out the unexplained differences, and does not claim that the step count causes the score mismatch.

fpdVersusViraNavsimProtocolCounts.fpdSource: FPD Appendix C describes NAVSIM v2 as 5,912 scenarios in 225 groups, each with two start frames 0.5 seconds apart, followed by stage/start/group aggregation.
fpdVersusViraNavsimProtocolCounts.viraSource: ViRA Appendix B.1 describes navtest as 12,146 real scenarios and navhard as 244 challenging real scenarios plus 4,164 synthetic follow-up scenarios.
fpdVersusViraNavsimProtocolCounts.assessment: The two navhard counts are not interchangeable and the reports do not normalize them into one claimed protocol. FPD explicitly warns that its count differs from other papers; ViRA attributes its count to its own fixed source. No unsupported reconciliation is asserted.

selectOccFlowPdfHtmlFigureNumbers.assessment: Direct PDF text and image inspection confirm PDF Figures 2 and 4 correspond to HTML Figures 1 and 3. The report captions and explanations preserve both numbering systems.

validation.targetedReportChecks: PASS: strict JSON frontmatter parsed, id matched filename, exactly eight H2 headings, and exactly two existing official image references per report.
validation.npmRunValidateNotes: The repository-wide validator reports stale local-corpus counts/candidate dispositions in several content/reviews JSON files and the pending independentReview in content/digest-audits/2026-10-12.json. It did not report a direct parse, id, image, tag, or heading error for these three reports before stopping. These integration failures were not edited in this independent content review.

limitations: No model training, inference, checkpoint download, metric-cache run, or closed-loop experiment was executed; the reports themselves state this boundary.

The six image-byte claims are supported by matching the current files to the recorded original-download URL/hash manifest and by direct visual inspection; the remote image bytes were not downloaded a second time during this review.

Direct CVF page opens returned access errors in one web path, so formal metadata was cross-checked through search-indexed CVF primary pages and the locally saved formal PDFs. This did not prevent mechanism or publication-state verification.
The verdict is valid only for the exact report and image SHA-256 bindings above. Any content or image change requires a fresh review.
